title: Commitments & Marketplace Billing Intake Framework — ledger, prioritization, and SLA triggers
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: create a single-source intake framework and living ledger for non-bug enterprise billing requests (commitment changes, invoicing variations, marketplace fee adjustments, cost allocation queries). This ticket captures the decision rubric, routing rules, SLA triggers, acceptance criteria, and example flows so that CS, Finance, Sales, and Solutions Engineering can route requests consistently and PM can prioritize effectively.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Intake fields required for each request type (customer, contract id, current commitment, requested change, billing impact estimate, data sensitivity, legal sign-off required).
- Tiered prioritization matrix (Revenue at risk, frequency, implementation complexity, legal/CX exposure).
- Routing rules: auto-assign to Finance Ops for invoicing adjustments; to Account Exec + Solutions Eng for commitment renegotiations > $X/month; to Marketplace Product for fee policy changes.
- SLA triggers: immediate escalation for revenue-loss > $100k or compliance/contract breach; 72h response for standard invoicing adjustments; 2-week resolution window for commitment negotiations.
- Ledger schema (for internal tracking): request id, customer, request_type, priority_score, assigned_team, current_status, impact_estimate, resolution_notes, created_date, target_resolution_date. (Note: ledger representation is a canonical schema, stored in our internal Confluence + Asana mirror; engineering will later surface in Console/Support tooling.)

Decisions & trade-offs we made so far: 
- We will NOT require engineering changes for every invoicing change; many will be handled by Finance Ops as manual journal entries. This keeps throughput high, but requires stricter audit logs.
- Default prioritization weights: revenue impact (40%), customer_tier (25%), implementation_effort (20%), compliance_risk (15%). These weights are opinionated to favor revenue protection. We can revisit after 1 quarter.
- Marketplace fee policy changes will always include a 2-week review window and a mandatory legal checklist to avoid marketplace-wide regressions.

Acceptance criteria (for this ticket):
1) A single intake form template published (Confluence) and an example Zendesk macro created.
2) Prioritization matrix documented with scoring examples for 8 real historical requests.
3) Routing rules enumerated with clear ownership and escalation contacts.
4) Ledger schema published and a lightweight Google Sheet + Confluence table seeded with 12 sample entries.
5) Ops runbook for Finance Ops outlining manual invoicing adjustment steps, audit trail required, and owner for each step.

Links & artifacts: 
- Confluence draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/enterprise-billing/intake-framework (editable)
- Example spreadsheet ledger: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/billing-ledger-sample
- Historical ticket set used for scoring: https://linear.redwood.ai/queries/PM-billing-sample
- PR for Zendesk macros: https://github.com/redwood-inference/support-scripts/pull/234
- Finance playbook (private): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/Finance/ops-invoicing-playbook.pdf

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: Manual invoicing changes increase audit labor. Mitigation: require a standard PDF justification and receipt uploaded to the ledger; Finance Ops to perform weekly reconciliation.
- Risk: Over-indexing on revenue can deprioritize compliance. Mitigation: compliance_risk has a floor score that forces escalation when present.

Next steps (owners and dates):
- PM (Aisha) to finalize intake form and post Confluence draft by 2026-02-18.
- Finance Ops (Marta Liu) to validate manual invoicing checklist by 2026-02-22.
- Support (Diego) to create Zendesk macro and test in staging by 2026-02-25.
- ENG (assigned later) to define API hooks for ledger ingestion (spike ticket recommended).
- Stakeholder review meeting scheduled 2026-02-28 (invite: Sales, Finance, CS, Legal, Support).

Longer-term: integrate ledger with Console so Account Managers can see request status in customer view and so automated routing reduces manual handoffs. This will be tracked as a follow-up epic (PM-10650).
